In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

They greet their Lord, salute Him, attain nearness to Him, rejoice in drawing close to Him, and receive from Him praise, honour, kindness and exaltation. Woe, then, to peoples who ignored His greatness and did not measure Him with His true measure, and so hastened the punishment in a manner of challenge and testing. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 70, verses 19–35:

{19–21} This description applies to the human being as such. He described his original nature [al-asliyyah] as being halu' (anxious, impatient), and he explained the halu' by his saying: {When evil touches him, he is distressed (jaza'an)}. So he becomes distressed if poverty, sickness, or the loss of something he loves befalls him, whether wealth, family, or children, and he does not use patience (sabr) or contentment (ridha) with what God has decreed in that. {And when good touches him, he is stingy (manu'an)}: so he does not spend from what God has given him, and he does not thank God for His blessings and kindness. Thus he is distressed in adversity and withholds in prosperity.

{22–23} {Except those who pray}: those who are characterized by those traits. When good touches them, they give thanks to God and spend from what God has bestowed upon them, and when evil touches them, they are patient and seek reward (ihtisab). His saying in describing them: {who are constant in their prayer}; i.e., they persist in it at its times, with its conditions and its complements, and they are not like one who does not perform it, or who performs it at some times and not others, or who performs it in a deficient manner.

{24–25} {And those in whose wealth there is a known right}: such as zakat and voluntary charity. {For the beggar}: the one who presents himself to ask. {And the deprived}: this is the needy person who does not ask people so that they give to him, and whose need is not noticed so that he may be given charity.

{26} {And those who affirm the Day of Judgment}; i.e., they believe in what God has reported and what the messengers have reported of recompense and resurrection, and they are certain of it, so they prepare for the Hereafter and strive for it as it deserves. Affirming the Day of Judgment necessarily entails affirming the messengers and what they brought of the scriptures.

They are unable to disobey the caller or turn away from the summons of the one who calls, but come humbled and subdued to stand before the Lord of the worlds. ﴿Their eyes downcast, humiliation overcoming them﴾: this is because abasement and anxiety have taken hold of their hearts and dominated their inner hearts, so their eyes have become downcast, their movements have stilled, and their voices have ceased. This state and this end is their Day ﴿which they were promised﴾, and the promise of God must certainly be fulfilled.

Completed. And praise be to God.
